title: Balanced Judgement in Speech and Columns

sections.content:
You know *en cambio*, *por el contrario*, *al contrario*, *no obstante* and *ahora bien* from B2 Unit 30. In opinion columns and spoken evaluation, these markers do the heavy lifting of weighing pros and cons without losing a clear conclusion.

A balanced paragraph often moves in three steps: first it concedes a point (with the concessive future, *pese a* or *todo hay que decirlo*), next it introduces a reservation or contrast (*ahora bien* for a decisive limit, *no obstante* for "nevertheless", *en cambio* for a side-by-side comparison, *por el contrario* for a direct opposite after a negative), and finally it sums up the verdict with *a fin de cuentas* ("at the end of the day").

Pay attention to punctuation and position: *ahora bien* and *no obstante* normally open a new clause after a full stop or semicolon and are followed by a comma. *Todo hay que decirlo* works parenthetically between commas to signal fairness before or after a concession.

sections.title: Weighing pros and cons in a column
rows: *El trazado, todo hay que decirlo, redujo los atascos.*
*El tranvía es puntual. Ahora bien, su rentabilidad tardará años.*
*Hubo sobrecostos; no obstante, la balanza se inclina a favor.*
Direct opposite after a negative (*por el contrario*)
*No empeoró el tráfico; por el contrario, despejó el centro.*
*A fin de cuentas, una ciudad no se mide solo por un presupuesto.*

items.spanish: El tranvía redujo el ruido en el centro. Ahora bien, el trazado dejó fuera dos barrios.
items.english: The tram reduced noise in the centre. That said, the route left out two neighbourhoods.

items.spanish: Las obras fueron lentas; no obstante, hoy casi nadie discute su utilidad.
items.english: The works were slow; nevertheless, today almost nobody disputes its usefulness.

items.spanish: El autobús tarda cuarenta minutos; el tranvía, en cambio, completa el recorrido en quince.
items.english: The bus takes forty minutes; the tram, on the other hand, completes the route in fifteen.

items.spanish: A fin de cuentas, conviene sopesar las molestias frente a las ventajas diarias.
items.english: At the end of the day, it is advisable to weigh up the inconveniences against the daily advantages.

sections.content: Do not confuse *en cambio* (comparing two different cases) with *por el contrario* (denying a claim and stating its opposite). And avoid putting a comma after *pero* or dropping the comma after *ahora bien* and *no obstante*.
